title: Rigveda
attributionNote: The Rigveda is an anonymous, collective corpus of hymns attributed by tradition to inspired seers (rishis). The catalogue does not assign a single author.
description: The oldest of the Vedas, in ten mandalas of hymns to Agni, Indra, Varuna, the Ashvins and other deities, together with the late tenth mandala and the Nasadiya hymn. Griffith's 1896 verse translation is imported hymn by hymn, each hymn a separately navigable section.
historicalContext: Composed in Vedic Sanskrit and transmitted orally with extraordinary fidelity before being written down. Griffith's translation (first edition 1889, second 1896) is a public-domain verse rendering; it is readable rather than a modern philological translation.
availabilityNote: Complete. All ten mandalas (1,028 hymns) of Griffith's translation are streamed from Wikisource at read time, one hymn per navigable section. The passage index follows the hymn and verse lines of the printed edition.
